references.text: Hail plague over Egypt where the Lord sent hail from heaven as judgment, a parallel to the stones that fell on the Amorites.
Describes hail mixed with fire falling from heaven, similar to divine intervention in Joshua 10:11.
The Lord thunders from heaven and sends hail and burning coals, a poetic description of God's heavenly weapons against enemies.
Reference to God destroying with hail, recalling God's use of hailstones as weapons.
God gave them hail instead of rain, showing God's use of natural forces as judgment.
Fire and hail are mentioned as elements that carry out God's word.
The Lord sends a mighty and powerful force like a hailstorm, a destructive storm.
The Lord lets His majestic voice be heard with hailstorms, a description of divine judgment.
Prophecy about large hailstones falling in wrath, similar to divine judgment.
God judges with pestilence, blood, torrential rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
Hail and fire mixed with blood are cast upon the earth, eschatological judgment with hail.
Large hail falls from heaven as part of God's judgment.
Great hail, weighing about a talent, fell from heaven on people, the ultimate hail judgment.
